A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The text, equations, algorithm boxes, and complete Appendices A–G are readable and support comparison across the revised definitions and renumbered results.

before.justification: V1 presents theoretical regret bounds, complexity bounds, and proofs. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: V2 revises the theoretical analysis but reports no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes, including in its appendices.

M1.justification: The ERM confidence-set construction and optimistic selection rules are retained, but prescribed confidence widths change: the general bandit coefficient b+c becomes 2b+c, while RL uses 3b+c and an additional H inside the logarithm. These alter the instantiated confidence sets; the new localisation remains an analysis device.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or experimentally evaluated scenarios. Bandits, logistic/Poisson models, and finite-horizon RL remain theoretical settings.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. Section 4.3 retains analytical comparisons with the bounds of Abeille et al. (2021) and Faury et al. (2022).

E3.justification: No empirical evaluation protocols, splits, metrics, or training budgets are introduced or revised. Changes to algorithm calibration and formal assumptions concern method and theory.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, or case studies. The appendix revisions concern mathematical proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. Revised analytical concentration guarantees are theoretical changes.

E6.justification: No empirical scores, observed trends, or experimental result entries are added, removed, or corrected. Changes to mathematical bounds and their constants are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Definition 2 replaces localisation through a restricted model class with a cap on eluder-sequence scales. The bandit and RL theorems consequently receive explicit localisation penalties and revised complexities. Appendix D adds a two-part control lemma; Appendix F introduces witness rescaling, requires convex parameter sets, and revises the logistic bound. Theorem 2 adds a positive-part curvature expression and an explicit deterministic instance. Appendices B–F also correct concentration, mixability, Hellinger, Taylor, and contraction arguments. RL assumptions now cover only F-indexed losses, and Proposition 26 newly asserts deterministic confidence-set containment.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list, and conclusion retain the same headline claims about the necessity of localisation, first-order bandit guarantees, and the first curvature-free leading-term RL guarantee.

C2.justification: Section 4 explains localisation through finite excess-loss scales instead of a uniformly restricted model neighbourhood. Section 4.1 replaces the broad assertion that the curvature ratio approximates κ in common GLMs with a sigmoid-specific exponential-growth statement. Existing discussions of Bernoullisation and one-sided small-cost guarantees remain.

D1.justification: Documented parameter prescriptions change, including the logistic confidence-width factor from 60(2S+1) to 60(3S+1) and the revised RL calibration. Appendix A's computational relaxation is retained; no code, data-access, hardware, or runtime information is added.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Section 1.1 are unchanged. However, Section 5.2 drops v1's explicit equivalence claim between its RL complexity and an ℓ1 Bellman eluder dimension of Jin et al. (2021), instead describing the revised stage-wise complexity as the RL analogue of the bandit quantity.

P1.justification: The central exposition and proof organisation are substantially rewritten. Section 4 replaces the model-subset narrative; Appendix D gains a separate D.1 proof; Appendix E reorganises supporting lemmas before the RL proof; and F.2 replaces the rogue-step subsection with witness construction. The overall section sequence and introductory framing remain.

P2.justification: The two algorithm boxes remain, with a small expansion and notation changes in Algorithm 2. Mathematical displays, section breaks, and the appendix contents are reformatted and reflowed. No figures or result tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's mismatch between globally localised model membership and action-wise deviation counts through scale-based control and witness rescaling, and repairs several loss and Taylor derivations. However, Appendix E's new Proposition 26 asserts deterministic confidence-set containment merely because the optimal Bellman update belongs to G. Membership does not establish proximity to the empirical minimum. V1 used G-indexed concentration for this step, whereas v2 removes that control. These substantial repairs coexist with an unsupported step underlying the central RL guarantee, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
